title: Justice Department Files to Intervene and Dismiss Lawsuit that Would Hamper America’s AI Innovation and Security

reading.body:
A power plant supplying electricity to an AI data center in Mississippi has faced a notice of intent to sue under the Clean Air Act for alleged violations of federal air quality standards. The facility operates without the required permits, according to reporting. Environmental groups and civil rights organizations have filed complaints asserting that pollution from the unpermitted plant falls disproportionately on nearby Black communities.

This is a case of infrastructure deployed to support AI computation without completing the regulatory process required for its environmental impact. The failure occurred at the power generation stage, before electricity reached the data center itself. Catching it would have required obtaining air quality permits and undergoing environmental review before beginning operations. It is not established whether the data center operator knew of the permitting violations or what the full scope of the alleged Clean Air Act breaches entails.

summary:
A notice of intent to sue has been filed regarding violations of the Clean Air Act at a gas turbine power plant located at 2875 Stanton Road S. in Southaven, Mississippi. This facility supplies power to xAI's Colossus II data center. The document indicates that environmental regulators have identified alleged violations of federal air quality standards at the power generation facility and are pursuing legal action against the operators.

The filing represents formal notification of the intent to pursue enforcement action under the Clean Air Act. While the specific violations and details are not clearly legible in the document, the legal notice represents a significant development for the power plant operations and its relationship with xAI's data center operations in the region.
